meaning: Teniendo todo en cuenta / A fin de cuentas
examples: All things considered, the product launch was a remarkable success.
He felt confident that, all things considered, he made the right decision.
All things considered, we managed to stay well within the budget.
Her recovery was swift and without complications, all things considered.
All things considered, it could have been a much worse outcome.

meaning: De hecho / En realidad
examples: I know him well; as a matter of fact, we attended the same university.
As a matter of fact, I was just about to call your office.
She didn't dislike the proposal; as a matter of fact, she endorsed it.
As a matter of fact, the flight leaves earlier than scheduled.
He has extensive experience in finance; as a matter of fact, he managed a hedge fund.

meaning: A toda costa / Cueste lo que cueste
examples: We must protect the integrity of the data at all costs.
He was determined to preserve the company's independence at all costs.
A security breach must be avoided at all costs.
They fought to preserve their basic civil rights at all costs.
We wanted to reach the mountain shelter before nightfall at all costs.

meaning: De vuelta al punto de partida / Empezar de cero
examples: When the investor pulled out, we were back to square one.
If this clinical trial fails, scientists will be back to square one.
The draft was rejected completely, sending us back to square one.
Rather than despairing at being back to square one, she restructured the plan.
A simple calculation error sent the entire engineering squad back to square one.

meaning: Estar equivocado de medio a medio / Ir tras la pista falsa
examples: If you think I took your laptop, you are barking up the wrong tree.
Detectives realized they had been barking up the wrong tree for weeks.
Blaming the junior staff means management is barking up the wrong tree.
He is barking up the wrong tree if he expects quick favors from me.
Scientific skepticism helps ensure researchers aren't barking up the wrong tree.

meaning: Andarse con rodeos / No ir al grano
examples: Stop beating around the bush and tell me what the real issue is.
He beat around the bush for ten minutes before asking for a raise.
A seasoned executive doesn't beat around the bush during evaluations.
Quit beating around the bush; did we secure the supply contract or not?
She appreciated people who spoke plainly instead of beating around the bush.

meaning: Hacer de tripas corazón / Afrontar un mal trago inevitable
examples: I decided to bite the bullet and schedule the long-overdue dental surgery.
The firm had to bite the bullet and announce painful staff cuts.
Instead of delaying the confrontation, she bit the bullet and called him.
You need to bite the bullet and admit your logistical mistake to the client.
We had to bite the bullet and replace the entire central heating system.

meaning: Un trago amargo / Una verdad o resultado difícil de aceptar
examples: Losing the tournament final by one point was a bitter pill to swallow.
Facing demotion after years of service was a bitter pill to swallow.
The austerity budget proved to be a bitter pill to swallow for citizens.
Admitting his thesis had foundational flaws was a bitter pill to swallow.
Failing the bar exam on the first attempt was a bitter pill to swallow.

meaning: No hay mal que por bien no venga / Una bendición encubierta
examples: Losing that dead-end job turned out to be a blessing in disguise.
The flight delay was a blessing in disguise, as we avoided severe turbulence.
Failing that initial interview proved to be a true blessing in disguise.
His ankle injury was a blessing in disguise because it allowed him to finish his book.
What seemed like a catastrophe initially was actually a blessing in disguise.

meaning: Romper el hielo / Superar la frialdad inicial en una reunión
examples: A warm, witty anecdote helped break the ice at the diplomatic conference.
Playing a casual party game is a great way to break the ice with strangers.
The facilitator started with an interactive exercise to break the ice.
Offering tea and biscuits helped break the ice during the negotiation.
He told an amusing travel story to break the ice with the hiring panel.

meaning: Trabajar o estudiar hasta altas horas de la noche
examples: Law students routinely burn the midnight oil before the bar exams.
She had to burn the midnight oil all week to finish the client proposal.
Burning the midnight oil regularly will eventually erode your health.
The entire software team burned the midnight oil to fix the critical bug.
He was visibly exhausted after burning the midnight oil for three days straight.

meaning: En líneas generales / En general
examples: By and large, the economic reforms have produced positive indicators.
The student population is, by and large, satisfied with campus housing.
By and large, it was an enjoyable and enlightening conference.
His technical arguments were, by and large, accepted by the committee.
By and large, the transition to remote working proceeded without major hitches.

meaning: Dar por terminada la jornada / Dejarlo por hoy
examples: We have covered enough agenda points; let's call it a day.
After ten hours of strenuous coding, the engineers decided to call it a day.
I'm too exhausted to think clearly; let's call it a day and resume tomorrow.
The rain won't stop, so the filming crew had to call it a day.
Once the last pallet was loaded onto the freighter, the crew called it a day.

meaning: Pillado con las manos en la masa / En flagrante
examples: The thief was caught red-handed as he slipped the diamond ring into his coat.
He was caught red-handed embezzling company funds through fake invoices.
The student was caught red-handed consulting hidden notes during the exam.
Security guards caught the trespassers red-handed inside the server room.
There was no point denying the accusation; he was caught red-handed.

meaning: Asimilar / Aceptar una realidad dolorosa o inevitable
examples: It took her years to come to terms with the loss of her older brother.
He must come to terms with the fact that his athletic career is over.
The nation had to come to terms with its complex historical legacy.
Therapy helped him come to terms with his underlying childhood anxieties.
She gradually came to terms with the permanent physical changes after surgery.

word: Cross that bridge when you come to it
meaning: Preocuparse por un problema cuando llegue el momento / No anticipar disgustos
examples: We might need extra funding next year, but we'll cross that bridge when we come to it.
Don't worry about potential zoning disputes; cross that bridge when you come to it.
She avoids unnecessary panic by crossing bridges only when she reaches them.
If the weather turns stormy tomorrow, we will cross that bridge when we come to it.
There's no point agonizing over hypotheticals; cross that bridge when you come to it.

meaning: Lamentarse por lo que ya no tiene remedio / A lo hecho, pecho
examples: The contract was awarded to a competitor, but there is no use crying over spilled milk.
Mistakes happen in research; don't cry over spilled milk and focus on the next test.
He dropped the antique vase, but he knew crying over spilled milk wouldn't repair it.
Focus on solutions rather than crying over spilled milk.
It's annoying that our flight was delayed, but crying over spilled milk won't change it.

meaning: Escatimar gastos o esfuerzos / Hacer las cosas a medias y de mala calidad
examples: Never cut corners when it comes to structural safety and aviation maintenance.
The developer cut corners on fireproofing materials, leading to disaster.
If you cut corners in your academic thesis, reviewers will easily spot it.
A master craftsman never cuts corners, even on parts invisible to the buyer.
The firm was penalized by regulators for cutting corners on clinical data reporting.

meaning: Abogado del diablo (adoptar un punto de vista contrario para suscitar debate)
examples: Let me play devil's advocate for a moment: what if consumer demand drops by half?
She often plays devil's advocate in board meetings to test the strength of arguments.
He wasn't genuinely opposing the initiative; he was just playing devil's advocate.
Playing devil's advocate helps uncover latent blind spots in strategic planning.
The professor acted as devil's advocate to compel students to defend their theses.

meaning: Con los pies en la tierra / Realista, humilde y accesible
examples: Despite her immense international fame, she remains remarkably down to earth.
I value his down to earth advice whenever I face complex life crossroads.
He is a wealthy philanthropist with a very pragmatic, down to earth attitude.
We need a down to earth strategy rather than idealistic, unfeasible projections.
Her down to earth demeanor made everyone feel immediately comfortable in her presence.

meaning: Poner un límite infranqueable / Establecer una frontera moral
examples: I support creative marketing, but I draw the line at deceptive advertising.
Parents need to know where to draw the line between guidance and overcontrol.
She draws the line at answering professional workplace emails on Sunday mornings.
The legal statute clearly draws the line between peaceful assembly and rioting.
He was willing to compromise on scheduling, but drew the line at wage cuts.

meaning: Del dicho al hecho hay un trecho / Más fácil decirlo que hacerlo
examples: Maintaining emotional composure in a crisis is definitely easier said than done.
Quitting a lifelong addictive habit is far easier said than done.
Starting a profitable enterprise from scratch is much easier said than done.
Telling someone to simply 'stop worrying' is always easier said than done.
Rebuilding trust after betrayal is honorable, but vastly easier said than done.

word: Every cloud has a silver lining
meaning: No hay mal que por bien no venga / Siempre hay un lado positivo
examples: The economic recession taught us fiscal prudence; every cloud has a silver lining.
He was grounded by injury, but wrote a brilliant screenplay; every cloud has a silver lining.
Don't lose hope after this setback; remember that every cloud has a silver lining.
The cancellation allowed us to spend precious time with family; every cloud has a silver lining.
Her failed business partnership showed her who her true friends were—every cloud has a silver lining.

meaning: Dar la cara / Afrontar las consecuencias de los propios actos
examples: After dodging questions for weeks, the director finally had to face the music.
He made a terrible accounting blunder and now must face the music before the board.
Don't run from your legal summons; stand up, face the music, and tell the truth.
She faced the music courageously and apologized for the organizational leak.
Sooner or later, every corrupt regime must face the music of public justice.

meaning: Escasos / Muy poco frecuentes / Raros de ver
examples: Opportunities of this magnitude are few and far between in our industry.
During the drought, rainfall was painfully few and far between.
Authentic leaders possessing genuine humility are few and far between.
Gas stations are few and far between along this stretch of desert highway.
Moments of quiet solitude were few and far between in the bustling dormitory.

meaning: Irse de las manos / Salirse de control
examples: The celebratory street gathering quickly got out of hand once fireworks were lit.
Establish firm ground rules early before workplace disputes get out of hand.
Inflation numbers got completely out of hand before monetary tightening occurred.
Her shopping habits were getting out of hand and accumulating dangerous debt.
Police stepped in decisively before the confrontation could get out of hand.

word: Give the benefit of the doubt
meaning: Dar el beneficio de la duda / Conceder credibilidad a falta de pruebas
examples: He claimed his alarm failed to go off, and I decided to give him the benefit of the doubt.
Unless there is concrete forensic evidence, we must give her the benefit of the doubt.
A healthy marriage requires giving your spouse the benefit of the doubt occasionally.
The committee gave the candidate the benefit of the doubt regarding the missing transcript.
Don't assume malicious intent immediately; give people the benefit of the doubt.

word: Hit the nail on the head
meaning: Dar en el clavo / Acertar de lleno
examples: Her diagnostic analysis of our operational bottleneck hit the nail on the head.
You hit the nail on the head when you identified communication as our core deficit.
His review of the philosophical treatise hit the nail on the head completely.
The editorial hit the nail on the head regarding the government's fiscal shortsightedness.
Marcus hit the nail on the head during the strategy briefing.

meaning: En pocas palabras / En resumen
examples: The proposed reform, in a nutshell, seeks to streamline public healthcare delivery.
Can you explain the plot of the novel to me in a nutshell?
In a nutshell, we are out of capital and need immediate debt restructuring.
His philosophical worldview, in a nutshell, is that voluntary struggle gives life meaning.
Here is the marketing plan in a nutshell: lower entry costs and emphasize reliability.

word: In the heat of the moment
meaning: En el calor del momento / En pleno arrebato
examples: He uttered harsh words in the heat of the moment that he later deeply regretted.
Try to pause before responding; don't make permanent promises in the heat of the moment.
In the heat of the moment, the referee blew the whistle prematurely.
She resigned in the heat of the moment after an intense argument with her manager.
Discipline means avoiding reckless physical reactions in the heat of the moment.

meaning: A largo plazo / Con el tiempo
examples: Investing in renewable energy infrastructure pays enormous dividends in the long run.
Short-term compromises with dishonest partners always backfire in the long run.
Learning touch-typing requires patience initially, but saves hours in the long run.
A lifestyle founded on personal integrity creates unshakable trust in the long run.
Preventative healthcare saves governments billions in the long run.

meaning: Echar un ojo / Vigilar de cerca a alguien o algo
examples: Could you keep an eye on my carry-on bag while I grab a coffee?
The pediatrician told us to keep a close eye on the toddler's fever.
Investors are keeping an eye on currency fluctuations ahead of the election.
Always keep an eye on your mirrors while overtaking heavy trucks on highways.
We must keep an eye on operational expenditures to prevent budget overruns.

word: Kill two birds with one stone
meaning: Matar dos pájaros de un tiro / Resolver dos asuntos a la vez
examples: By cycling to work, he kills two birds with one stone: getting fit and saving money.
Scheduling the client conference in Madrid killed two birds with one stone, as she visited family.
This innovative software kills two birds with one stone by automating invoicing and stock control.
I killed two birds with one stone by listening to educational audiobooks while jogging.
The municipal project killed two birds with one stone: flood control and creating a wetland park.

meaning: Por último, pero no por ello menos importante
examples: And last but not least, I want to express my deepest gratitude to my devoted family.
Last but not least, verify that all emergency exit doors remain unbolted.
Our final panelist, last but not least, is an acclaimed expert on marine biodiversity.
Last but not least, never underestimate the power of consistent daily habits.
He thanked the sponsors, the organizers, and, last but not least, the dedicated volunteers.

meaning: Mover cielo y tierra / Remover hasta la última piedra para lograr algo
examples: Detectives promised to leave no stone unturned in their search for the missing heir.
Our research team will leave no stone unturned in finding the root cause of the error.
She left no stone unturned when preparing her defense for the Supreme Court.
The archaeological expedition left no stone unturned across the ancient desert plateau.
To secure funding for the hospital wing, the board left no stone unturned.

word: Let the cat out of the bag
meaning: Irse de la lengua / Revelar un secreto sin querer
examples: It was supposed to be a surprise birthday party, but Marcus let the cat out of the bag.
Don't let the cat out of the bag regarding our confidential acquisition plans.
She accidentally let the cat out of the bag during a casual corridor chat.
Once the press let the cat out of the bag, the minister had to deliver a statement.
I trusted him with our secret, but he immediately let the cat out of the bag.

meaning: Para no hacer el cuento largo / En resumidas cuentas
examples: To make a long story short, our car broke down, but we reached the church on time.
Make a long story short: did the bank approve the commercial mortgage or not?
To make a long story short, they settled the property dispute out of court.
He rambled on for an hour before finally making a long story short.
To make a long story short, we decided to sell the rural farm and move to Madrid.

meaning: Llegar a fin de mes / Cuadrar las cuentas domésticas
examples: With inflation rising steadily, many working families struggle to make ends meet.
He worked two jobs throughout college just to make ends meet.
After losing his primary client, it became nearly impossible to make ends meet.
Budgeting carefully each week helped the young couple make ends meet.
Pensions must keep pace with living expenses so the elderly can make ends meet.

meaning: Perder el tren / Dejar pasar una oportunidad irrepetible
examples: If you don't submit your university grant application today, you will miss the boat.
Traditional bookstores that ignored e-commerce completely missed the boat.
He missed the boat on investing in tech stocks during the early digital boom.
Act decisively when market openings emerge, or you will miss the boat entirely.
Don't wait until all early-bird tickets sell out and miss the boat.

meaning: El que algo quiere, algo le cuesta / Sin esfuerzo no hay recompensa
examples: The physical coach kept shouting 'no pain, no gain' during the grueling interval sprints.
Mastering complex legal analysis demands long hours—no pain, no gain.
Muscles need to be pushed beyond comfort to grow stronger: no pain, no gain.
Learning a foreign language requires enduring awkward communicative errors; no pain, no gain.
Achieving high-level musical mastery is rigorous—no pain, no gain.

meaning: No es para tanto / No tiene gran importancia
examples: Don't worry about being ten minutes late; it's really not a big deal.
Spilling some tea on the kitchen tile is not a big deal; it wipes clean easily.
He made a minor grammar slip, but in conversational speech, it's not a big deal.
Why are you shouting over a cracked plastic bowl? It is not a big deal.
Missing one evening gym session due to exhaustion is not a big deal.

word: Off the top of my head
meaning: Así a bote pronto / De memoria y sin consultar datos
examples: Off the top of my head, I'd say the renovation will cost around twenty thousand euros.
I can't recall the exact case citation off the top of my head, but I'll check the library.
Off the top of my head, there were about fifty attendees at the annual gala.
Can you name the capital of Kazakhstan off the top of your head?
Off the top of my head, our firm has eleven active infrastructure contracts.

meaning: Indeciso / En terreno neutral sin decantarse por una postura
examples: Many undecided voters are still on the fence just days before the ballot.
I am on the fence about whether to accept the job in London or stay in Madrid.
Management remained on the fence regarding the proposed remote-work policy.
You cannot stay on the fence forever; this ethical dilemma demands a clear stance.
She was on the fence about purchasing the vintage convertible due to maintenance costs.

meaning: En la misma sintonía / De acuerdo en objetivos y criterios
examples: Before we launch the advertising blitz, let's make sure the whole team is on the same page.
A weekly briefing ensures that sales and manufacturing remain on the same page.
Partners need to be on the same page regarding long-term financial budgeting.
We had a forty-minute video conference to ensure both departments were on the same page.
It is impossible to navigate a crisis smoothly unless leadership is on the same page.

meaning: De pascuas a ramos / En contadísimas ocasiones
examples: He lives in Australia, so we only see him once in a blue moon.
Snow falls in this coastal Mediterranean city only once in a blue moon.
I enjoy a rich chocolate pastry, but I only eat it once in a blue moon.
A talent of this extraordinary caliber appears in athletics only once in a blue moon.
He is usually calm; he loses his temper once in a blue moon.

meaning: De la nada / Caído del cielo / De forma totalmente inesperada
examples: Out of the blue, my childhood best friend phoned me after twenty years of silence.
The devastating corporate layoff announcement came completely out of the blue.
A sudden torrential rainstorm developed out of the blue over the sunny valley.
She received a generous international job offer entirely out of the blue.
The engine seized up out of the blue while we were cruising along the highway.

meaning: Pan comido / Algo sumamente fácil de realizar
examples: Don't worry about the driving theory exam; with proper review, it's a piece of cake.
Replacing a blown fuse in this electrical panel is an absolute piece of cake.
For an experienced programmer, building this basic landing page was a piece of cake.
He thought passing the fitness test would be a piece of cake, but he struggled.
Translating that short commercial brochure was a piece of cake for her.

meaning: Tomar el pelo a alguien en broma
examples: Don't panic; I didn't actually lose your wedding ring, I was just pulling your leg.
Are you serious about winning the national lottery, or are you pulling my leg?
My grandfather loved to pull our legs with tall tales about arctic adventures.
She realized he was pulling her leg when he started grinning mischievously.
Stop pulling my leg and tell me what the doctor actually said.

meaning: Estar plenamente de acuerdo / Compartir la misma visión
examples: My father and I rarely see eye to eye on modern architecture and design.
The union and the municipal board finally saw eye to eye on pensions.
It is difficult to manage a joint venture if co-founders do not see eye to eye.
They argued frequently, but on core ethical values, they saw eye to eye.
We don't always see eye to eye on tactical steps, but our overarching aim is identical.

word: Take it with a grain of salt
meaning: Tomar con reservas / No creerse algo al pie de la letra
examples: Take celebrity political endorsements with a grain of salt.
He tends to exaggerate his achievements, so take his war stories with a grain of salt.
Online forum reviews should always be taken with a healthy grain of salt.
She listened attentively to the rumor, but took it with a grain of salt.
Take early poll numbers with a grain of salt until verified by independent data.

meaning: Una cucharada de tu propia medicina
examples: The arrogant debater finally got a taste of his own medicine when his flaws were exposed.
She spent months interrupting colleagues, but didn't enjoy a taste of her own medicine.
The aggressive corporate competitor received a taste of its own medicine in court.
Giving a notorious gossip a taste of their own medicine rarely resolves the core issue.
He was forced to endure a taste of his own medicine after treating juniors harshly.

word: The ball is in your court
meaning: La pelota está en tu tejado / Te toca mover ficha a ti
examples: We have made our final financial settlement offer; now the ball is in your court.
I sent you all the revised architectural drafts; the ball is in your court.
She told him the ball was in his court regarding where they would spend Christmas.
The regulatory agency completed its review; the ball is in the manufacturer's court.
I have apologized sincerely; the ball is in her court to decide if we reconcile.

meaning: La punta del iceberg / Solo una mínima parte visible de un problema mayor
examples: The initial accounting discrepancies were merely the tip of the iceberg of corporate fraud.
Reported cyberattack attempts represent only the tip of the iceberg in digital warfare.
These symptoms are just the tip of the iceberg; we need comprehensive blood tests.
The thirty arrested street smugglers are just the tip of the iceberg of the global cartel.
What the public saw was the tip of the iceberg; behind closed doors, chaos reigned.

meaning: Poco indispuesto / Ligeramente enfermo o desganado
examples: I am feeling a bit under the weather today, so I will work from home.
She looked pale and under the weather during the morning department meeting.
A warm bowl of chicken soup is wonderful when you feel under the weather.
He stayed home from university because he was feeling slightly under the weather.
Drink plenty of water and rest if you feel under the weather after vaccination.

meaning: Agua pasada / Asuntos pasados que ya no guardan rencor
examples: We had our fierce differences years ago, but that is all water under the bridge now.
Don't worry about the broken contract; it's water under the bridge, let's move forward.
Past romantic rivalries became water under the bridge as they matured into adulthood.
Life is too brief to dwell on old grudges; treat them as water under the bridge.
The settlement was signed, and both parties agreed past disputes were water under the bridge.
